terms.title: Terms of service
terms.summary: LabTrack MN is a tool to organise and keep your test results, medicines and treatments. It gives no diagnosis or treatment advice — ask your doctor about health questions.
terms.body: The app is for organising, storing and reviewing information, reminders you set up, and sharing with people you choose. It does not suggest medicine doses, check drug interactions or interpret results. Only your organisation's admin creates accounts; you set your own password and the admin never knows it. You can delete your account at any time in Settings.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: Explains who is responsible for your data, where it is kept, who it is shared with and for how long.
privacy.body: The data controller is the company that provides the app. Data is kept on servers in Mongolia and sent over encrypted connections. Admins cannot see your health information — only in a documented emergency approved by two admins, which then shows in the admin history in the app. Data is passed only to people you allow (doctor, caregiver) and to contracted providers needed to run the service (hosting, SMS, notifications; and the AI service if you allow AI). You have the right to see, correct and delete your data. After you ask to delete your account, data is erased for good after 30 days; backup copies expire within a limited time. Copies you have already shared yourself (PDFs, etc.) cannot be recalled by us.

sensitive_data.title: Processing health information
sensitive_data.summary: Test results, medicines and transplant details are sensitive data under the law, so separate consent is needed.
sensitive_data.body: Under the Law on Personal Data Protection, health information is sensitive data. You agree that the results, medicines, treatments and transplant details you enter are processed only for this app's service (storing, organising, charts, reminders, sharing). If you withdraw this consent, the app can no longer be used; what you entered stays stored and you can have your account deleted.

ai.title: Read results with AI
ai.summary: Photos and PDFs of your results are sent to an AI service in the USA (Anthropic Claude) to read the values automatically. Without this, you enter values by hand.
ai.body: This consent has two parts: (1) processing documents with AI, and (2) transferring data outside Mongolia (to the USA). Values read by the AI are stored as a draft; they appear in charts and summaries only after you check and confirm them (a value that may need urgent attention is flagged before that). How long the provider keeps sent documents is set out in the privacy policy. You can withdraw at any time; from then on no document is sent abroad, but documents already sent cannot be recalled.

caregiver.title: Sharing with caregivers
caregiver.summary: Someone you invite (a caregiver) can see your profile, add records and be notified when a dose has not been logged yet.
caregiver.body: You invite a caregiver by username; they can access your profile only after they accept the invitation. A caregiver can see your lab results, medicines, transplant and emergency card information and add records; they cannot share or delete. They are notified when a dose has not been logged yet. You can pause a caregiver's notifications or end their access at any time. Withdrawing this consent ends every caregiver's access and every pending invitation at once; to share again, you invite anew. What a caregiver has already seen or copied cannot be taken back.

about.title: About the app
about.purpose: LabTrack MN helps people who have had an organ transplant keep their health information in order, store and follow it, get the medicine reminders they set themselves, record the doses they take, keep an emergency card and share with a caregiver they choose.
about.notTitle: What this app does not do
about.not: It does not diagnose, does not suggest treatment or medicine doses, and does not check medicine interactions. It does not replace your doctor's advice. Talk to your doctor before you change or stop a medicine.
about.reliability: Medicine reminders can come late or not at all because of phone settings or battery saving. Caregiver notifications are not guaranteed either. Take your medicines on time as your doctor told you.
about.emergency: If you suddenly feel much worse, call 103 or go to the nearest hospital. The app's reminders and notifications do not replace emergency care.

trends.title: Trends
trends.empty: No confirmed lab results yet. Trends appear here once you add and confirm results.

trends.chartLabel: Trend chart of {name}, {count} results. Every value is in the list below.
trends.legend: Thin grey steps: the reference range printed on each result (it may change with the lab). Red dashed: the critical limit printed on the result. Point shapes: ● within range, ▲ outside range, ◆ critical, hollow - no range, or a "<"/">" value. Dotted vertical lines: transplant, events.
trends.legendDose: Dashed steps (right axis): the recorded daily dose of {medicine}.
trends.doseNote: Doses are shown as recorded. Your doctor interprets how dose and results relate; talk to your doctor about any dose change.
trends.truncated: The latest {limit} results are shown. Choose a shorter period.
trends.doseNotDrawn: Doses planned ahead, on a weekly schedule or in another unit are not on the chart - they are in the dose history.
trends.notDrawn: Not on the chart (the unit cannot be converted)

timeline.pickTwo: Choose the two results to compare from the list.

shares.title: Share with a doctor or viewer

Only after they accept can they view this whole profile (results, medicines, transplant, vitals, timeline) — they cannot add, change, delete or share anything further. You can revoke it at any time. What they have already seen or copied cannot be taken back.

acceptBody.viewer: You will be able to view this profile. You cannot change, add or share anything; the days you open it are shown to the profile's owner.

leave.rowHint: Leave a profile shared with you
leave.title: Stop viewing this profile?

The link works until the chosen time ends, the number of opens is reached, or you revoke it. What was already seen or copied cannot be taken back.

created.qrLabel: QR code of the share link

created.urlLabel: Share link (same as the QR code)

clinician.rowHint: Lab targets and notes from your doctor
clinician.intro: Lab targets and notes from a doctor you shared your profile with appear here. Only the doctor writes them. Ask your doctor if you have questions.
clinician.introDoctor: You can write targets and notes on this profile. The owner and the people it is shared with see them under your name. The app only marks values against the target.

level.title: Tacrolimus level (numbers)
level.what: Mean, variability (CV% = standard deviation ÷ mean × 100) and the number of values inside the doctor's target, from confirmed tacrolimus results. Only values from {months} months after the transplant (from its latest possible day when only the month or year is known), with an exact number, and the first value of each day count.
level.notAVerdict: Numbers only — the app gives no threshold, judgement or dose suggestion.

reason.no_transplant: Not calculated: no transplant date is recorded.
reason.too_few: Not enough values to calculate (at least 5 are needed).
reason.zero_mean: No number can be calculated from these values.
reason.no_unit: Not calculated: this test has no unit in the catalog.

leftOut.bounds_left_out: {n} left out: a bound such as "< 2", not an exact number
leftOut.early_left_out: {n} left out: within {months} months of the transplant
leftOut.same_day_left_out: {n} left out: a second value on the same day

level.labsMixed: Values come from different labs ({labs}) — their methods may differ, which can affect CV%.
level.labUnknown: {n, plural, one {# value has} other {# values have}} no lab named — it may come from another lab.

targets.title: Doctor's targets

targets.none: No targets set by a doctor.
targets.endBody: The target ends today. Earlier values keep their marks.

form.title: New target
form.order: The lower limit cannot be above the upper limit.

notes.title: Doctor's notes
notes.newHint: The owner and the people the profile is shared with see it under your name.

steroid.title: Steroid emergency card
steroid.what: Long use of steroids (such as prednisolone) can lead to adrenal insufficiency. When marked, the emergency card shows a warning. A doctor decides whether it is needed — the app does not infer it from the medicines.
steroid.threshold: NHS England National Patient Safety Alert 2020 (NatPSA/2020/005/NHSPS) and Society for Endocrinology guidance: a steroid emergency card is advised after prednisolone ≥ 5 mg/day (or an equivalent steroid) for ≥ 4 weeks; ≥ 40 mg/day for more than 1 week; ≥ 3 short high-dose courses within 12 months; high-dose inhaled or topical steroids and injections may also count. The risk lasts up to 12 months after stopping. The app does not infer this from the medicines — you decide. When marked, the patient's emergency card shows a warning.
steroid.ownerHint: Mark it if your doctor told you that you need a steroid emergency card.
steroid.markedBySelf: Marked by the patient on their doctor's advice ({date}).
steroid.markBody: The emergency card will show the “Steroid emergency card” warning.
steroid.clearBody: The steroid warning is removed from the emergency card.

export.fhirHint: FHIR is the international standard health systems use to exchange data.
